sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A bulbous wild leek native from Macaronesia and the Mediterranean region to Central Asia, also grown in several cultivated forms, including leek. Plants may reach 1.5 m; flat, V-shaped leaves can be 50 × 7 cm, and the spherical flower umbel 4–12 cm across. It often grows on rocky ground near coasts.

sections.title: Food and comparison
sections.text: Bulbs and leaves are used as vegetables in cultivated forms. Horticultural group limits vary. Compared with the common onion (Allium cepa), this species has flat leaves and includes leek-type crops; onion leaves are hollow and cylindrical and the crop is selected for its bulb.
